title: Correlation Bookmarking & Selective Span Folding — Threadline Drill Prototype
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Design and prototype a focused ‘threadline drill’ for the Redwood Console trace view that lets engineers bookmark correlation IDs, selectively fold/unfold spans (by reason and severity), and persist view state per-user. This is intended as a lightweight drill-in experience from dashboards or trace search results for fast RCA and cost/latency attribution.
goals: Enable users to pin or bookmark a correlation ID from a trace list and open a minimized drill with contextual actions
Support selective span folding by category (database, network, model-inference) and by severity (errors/warnings) to reduce visual noise
Persist per-user view state: bookmarks, collapsed groups, and time-range selection
Provide quick filters and keyboard-first interactions for fast navigation
Integrate a small cost/latency strip that surfaces token-related cost hints for infer-heavy spans
acceptance_criteria: Prototype demonstrates bookmarking flow from trace list to drill modal and persisting bookmarks in user settings
Users can collapse/expand span groups and individual spans; collapsed state is saved per-user
Filters include span-type toggles, severity toggles, and a text search for span metadata (host, kernel, correlation id)
Design passes accessibility review: keyboard nav, focus states, screen-reader labels for bookmarks and fold controls
Engineering has validated render strategy for traces up to 2k spans without UI jank in the prototype harness
design_notes: Primary surface is a right-side ‘drill’ panel that overlays the Console trace list; alternative is full-screen when user presses Enter
Bookmark affordance: small pin icon beside correlation ID; bookmarked items appear in a persistent ‘Pinned Correlations’ shelf in the Console sidebar

Span folding model: two layers — categorical group collapse (e.g., DB calls) and inline single-span fold; collapsed spans render a summary row with metrics (count, total time, token cost if inference)
Animations: use height/opacity transitions with prefers-reduced-motion support; folding animations must be under 120ms for perceived snappiness
Cost strip: inline micro-chart showing token count and estimated USD cost for inference spans, with a tooltip linking to Optimize recommendations
Keyboard shortcuts: ‘b’ to toggle bookmark, ‘f’ to open filter bar, arrow keys to navigate spans, space to toggle collapse
Edge cases: very long span names should truncate with full title on hover; missing correlation IDs should show ‘unattributed’ and allow temporary grouping by request path
Data requirements for engineering: endpoints to fetch spans with grouping hints and pre-computed token counts OR a lightweight estimation function in frontend when server data is unavailable
engineering_feedback: ENG: initial feedback (2026-02-17) — prefer server-side group summaries for performance; client estimation acceptable as fallback
ENG: render note (2026-02-24) — need a virtualized list for spans >500; suggested react-window with sticky group headers
ENG: API ask (2026-03-03) — add correlation bookmark endpoints (POST/DELETE /user/bookmarks) and a persisted collapse state endpoint
ENG: security note (2026-03-08) — bookmarks are user-scoped only, avoid exposing bookmarked correlation IDs in org-level analytics by default
review_comments: PM (Lena Fischer) — like the bookmark shelf idea; asked for a quick mock of mobile behavior
Infra (Diego Torres) — requested metrics to quantify cost-strip accuracy; link to Optimize evaluation needed
Design lead (Nora Kim) — suggested stronger affordance on collapsed-summary rows to surface why spans were folded (reason tag)
Accessibility reviewer (Samir Patel) — requested ARIA labels for collapse buttons and verification of tab order in prototype
decisions: Persist bookmarks and collapsed groups per-user rather than org-wide (keeps privacy & reduces accidental exposure)
Use a right-drawer drill overlay by default; full-screen for ‘deep dive’ keyboard action
Show estimated cost for inference spans only when token metadata is available; otherwise show ‘estimation unavailable’ tooltip
Favor server-provided group summaries, with a client-side fallback for older model backends
next_steps: Finalize visual treatment for collapsed-summary rows (label + micro-metrics)
Add mobile/responsive mocks and hand off to frontend for an initial spike
Sync with Optimize team to define token-cost estimation contract
Schedule design review with accessibility owner and product manager before engineering kickoff
